subject: science
domain: Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

items.prompt:
Many trait distributions, like height, form a
A) bell shape
B) straight line up
C) single point
D) square

steps: Many traits form a bell-shaped distribution.

items.prompt:
In a bell-shaped distribution, most individuals are
A) near the average
B) at the extremes
C) missing
D) identical

steps: Most individuals are near the average.

items.prompt:
The average of a trait tells you the
A) typical value in the population
B) rarest value
C) color
D) weather
items.answer: A) typical value in the population

steps: The average is the typical value.

items.prompt:
Probability can describe the
A) chance of inheriting a trait
B) color of the sky
C) time of day
D) weight of a rock
items.answer: A) chance of inheriting a trait

steps: Probability gives the chance of inheriting a trait.

items.prompt:
A statistic that describes how spread out values are is the
A) spread (variation)
B) name
C) color
D) date

steps: Spread measures how far values are from the average.

items.prompt:
Two populations have the same average length but different spreads. They are
A) different distributions
B) identical
C) impossible
D) the same individual

Why is the average alone not always enough to describe a trait?
A) Two populations can share an average but differ in spread
B) Averages are never useful
C) Traits do not vary
D) Spread is always zero
items.answer: A) Two populations can share an average but differ in spread

steps: Spread adds information the average misses.

items.prompt:
Statistics and probability together describe traits by
A) summarizing current variation and predicting inherited trait chances
B) changing the traits
C) ignoring the data
D) only naming the traits
items.answer: A) summarizing current variation and predicting inherited trait chances

steps: Together they describe and predict the distribution.
